scope: Proposition 6.9 (Fixed normalized inputs in a varying-label diagonal) of the manuscript “Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps” (preprints/Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritical-FK-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e7dab39caf778176), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 46. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let vr > 0 be deterministic volume labels. For each r, take an unconditioned joint law supplied by Theorem 6.1, re-expressed in the units of (6.14). Suppose its base field in those units has one fixed ordinary normalized reference law, including the same imaginary-field law with uniform phase. Draw the observation marks using the same normalized convention at every row. A joint diagonal may retain every fixed relative offset in a countable list, provided every retained effective microscopic time unit tends to infinity. The output denominators may be arbitrary deterministic positive numbers. The resulting limits have the compatible kernels and the conditional product property of Theorem 6.1, and may retain fixed measurable continuum functionals and the all-order arrays of Theorem 6.6.
